thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: org=polaris-health exceeded sustained request QPS threshold (p99 latency > 2.5s, error-rate spike). Auto-throttle engaged for org-specific bucket. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.io/telemetry/orgs/polaris-health

Alex C: looking at it — seeing a big tail of multimodal calls with long context and beam-rerank. p50 ok, p99 terrible. Can someone confirm top endpoints?

Tess R: confirmed. `chat.generate` + `embed.create` combos from polaris-health are causing large KV cache pressure. They also have a couple of long streaming sessions.

Alex C: cc @Mari V @Lina (CS) @Raj P — this is customer-impacting. Are they on Dedicated or Hosted?

Lina (CS): they're on Hosted with enterprise quotas. Customer reported intermittent 503s ~5m ago. They pushed a high-traffic feature at 15:40 UTC.

Mari V: I can pull their recent request histogram. ETA 2m.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T15:42:10Z — rollout check: no recent infra deploys to serving runtime in last 30m.

Mari V: quick dump: majority calls are `chat.generate` with long system prompts + doc-reranker calls. Average tokens per request ~1.8k for the last 10m.

Alex C: options: 1) temporary org-level rate uplift (increase QPS) 2) tighten per-org concurrency to reduce KV thrash 3) route their long calls to a slower, more-resilient model variant 4) ask customer to pause feature. I'm leaning 1+3 for immediate mitigation while we stabilize. Thoughts?

Tess R: agree. My concern with pure uplift is it may overload shared KV/worker pools and cause cross-org impact. Better to route heavy requests to `gptx-serve-slow` variant (more memory, lower perf) and apply a soft concurrency cap.

Alex C: plan then: a) enable temporary model-route for polaris-health to `gptx-serve-slow` for requests > 1000 tokens b) bump org QPS by 1.5x for 20m c) set concurrency cap to 10 per org to stop bursts.

Raj P: I'll prepare the customer message. We should avoid exposing internal details — will say we're applying a temporary traffic routing to stabilize latencies and will update in 20 minutes.

Tess R: executing mitigation now. Running command:```bash
rbctl org adjust-routing --org polaris-health --match "tokens>1000" --target-model gptx-serve-slow --duration 20m
rbctl org adjust-qps --org polaris-health --factor 1.5 --duration 20m
rbctl org set-concurrency --org polaris-health --limit 10 --duration 20m
```

Alex C: :eyes: ping when done. Also start sampling traces for 1% of their requests.

Tess R: routing change applied. QPS bump applied. Concurrency cap set. Trace sampling enabled. Metrics: p99 dropping from 2.6s -> 1.2s within 90s. Error rate trending down.

Lina (CS): messaged customer (Polaris Health): "We're applying a temporary traffic reroute and stabilizing measures; this should reduce errors. We'll follow up in 20 minutes with status." They replied: "Thanks — will pause non-critical jobs."

Alex C: nice. I'll stay on it for now. @Tess R can you monitor for any cross-org regression?

Tess R: will watch dashboards and set an alert if any other org p99 > 2s for >3m.

Mari V: captured traces and flamegraphs, creating an incident ticket for postmortem. Putting current snapshot in #incidents-pivots board.

deploy-bot: note: ephemeral changes applied (rbctl audit id=a8f3c2).

Tess R: halfway through window (10m): polaris error-rate at 0.6% (was 4.3%), p99 stable ~1.1s. No regressions observed across top 50 orgs.

Alex C: ok preparing handoff. I'm going offline in ~8m. Next oncall @Tess R takes lead. Handoff notes: routing+qps+concurrency applied until 15:63 UTC (20m), traces sampled, customer notified, follow-up PM ticket for model optimization and recommended limits.

Tess R: taking it. I'll extend if needed. If we need a longer mitigation window, we should convert to a scheduled change and escalate to infra for capacity adjustments.

Lina (CS): customer asked for a short summary for their tech team. Raj — can you send a 1-paragraph summary?

Raj P: sending now: "We observed elevated latency and errors due to a burst of long-context requests. We applied a temporary routing of long requests to a more memory-optimized model and modestly increased QPS for 20 minutes while setting a concurrency cap to mitigate KV cache pressure. Monitoring shows improved latency and reduced errors. We'll follow up with recommended config and a timeline for permanent changes."

Alex C: thanks. Final update before I drop: telemetry looks stable, resources within normal utilization, recommend 1) backend model tune 2) guidance to polaris on batching/streaming changes 3) postmortem to engineer follow-ups.

Tess R: marking the mitigation as successful for the window. I'll keep an eye for the next 30m and extend if we see drift.

incident-bot: Incident note appended: id=INC-2026-1871234567, severity=sev2, mitigation=org routing+qps+concurrency, owner=Tess R, cs_contact=Lina (CS).

Alex C: :white_check_mark: closing my shift. Thanks team.

Lina (CS): customer replied: "All good now, thanks for the quick response."

Mari V: created postmortem stub: https://docs.redwood.io/pm/incidents/INC-2026-1871234567 — assigning action items.

Tess R: last check (15m after mitigation): p99 0.9s, errors <0.5%, will finalize postmortem later today.

Alex C: appreciated everyone.

Raj P: adding CS follow-up: schedule a short sync with customer to discuss long-term request shaping next week.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation; follow-ups tracked in incident ticket. :lock:
